html:
The overthrow of Kwame Nkrumah by the army and police on 24 February 1966, while he was on a trip to Beijing and Hanoi.

Nkrumah had made Ghana a one-party state, jailed opponents without trial and spent heavily as cocoa prices fell. The plotters, who formed the National Liberation Council, were cheered in the streets; Western governments welcomed the coup. Nkrumah went into exile in Guinea, as guest of Sekou Toure, and died in 1972. Ghana then swung between civilian and military rule until Jerry Rawlings and the 1992 constitution.
sum: The overthrow of Kwame Nkrumah by the army and police on 24 February 1966, while he was on a trip to Beijing and Hanoi.
